title: Chopin, Nocturne Op. 27 No. 2: Pachmann and Lévy
work: Nocturne in D♭ major, Op. 27 No. 2
question: Pachmann and Lévy each play two voices with one hand.
intro: The first D♭ major melody is a single line above an accompaniment of broken left-hand figures. The right hand soon adds a second voice in thirds and sixths, and the melody is more heavily ornamented at each return.

recordings.label: Vladimir de Pachmann, 1925
recordings.note: Pachmann plays his own Baldwin at Hayes, with extra notes in bars 30–32.

recordings.label: Frank Lévy, c. 2014
recordings.note: Lévy’s teachers included Maria Tipo and Leon Fleisher; this nocturne comes from his Musopen Chopin project.

passages.label: Opening melody
passages.note: The melody begins on F above broken chords in D♭ major. The right hand holds long notes over six-note figures in the left hand.

passages.label: Melody in thirds
passages.note: The right hand plays the melody in thirds as the bass moves towards B♭ minor.

passages.label: First return of the melody
passages.note: F returns above a low D♭. The opening melody returns, with new ornaments on its long notes.

passages.label: Third statement of the melody
passages.note: The melody returns for the third time; its continuation becomes a long flourish that climbs and falls across the keyboard.

passages.label: Coda over a D♭ pedal
passages.note: The bass holds D♭ while pairs of notes descend above it, marked dolcissimo — very sweetly.
